  Terse gloss: "Hepher, a proper masculine name borne by a Manassite clan-head, a Judahite, and one of David's warriors"
  Readable gloss: "Hepher (sometimes transliterated Chepher) is a personal name appearing across several genealogical and military contexts. A Manassite descendant of Gilead, Hepher fathered Zelophehad whose daughters famously petitioned for inheritance rights (Num 26:32-33; 27:1; Josh 17:2-3). The name also belongs to a son of Ashur in the Judahite genealogy (1 Chr 4:6) and possibly one of David's mighty warriors (1 Chr 11:36), though that text is disputed. The Septuagint renders it Opher or Aphar, reflecting varied transliteration traditions."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "Hepher (personal name)"
    Enriched: The proper name Hepher (חֵפֶר), used of at least three distinct individuals: primarily the Manassite clan-founder whose lineage includes Zelophehad's daughters (Num 26:32; Josh 17:2), a Judahite in the Ashur genealogy (1 Chr 4:6), and a warrior listed among David's heroes (1 Chr 11:36). English glosses render it 'Hepher' or 'Chepher,' while Spanish uses 'Jefer/Hefer,' reflecting the guttural het.
    Existing Spanish translations: Héfer, Jefer, Jéfer, y-Héfer
